pov.mode: close third, past tense — the series' established voice: the cataloguing narrator (counts things, names places precisely), diegetic documents in italics with their own plain first-person register (the Power Log), emotion through procedure and objects, dry oblique dialogue, PG-13, no modern idiom. READER STANDARD: written for a thirteen-year-old — clean language (no profanity, crude slang or oaths), moral goodness (honest, courageous, loyal, restrained conduct; wrong named as wrong; cruelty never rewarded), violence with cost and no gore, no sexual content.
knowledge_boundary: Cael is nineteen; days 286–288 (the archive week's middle); the party down each day by count, out by the bell; the clerk has looked at them twice; cash 136.

RUNE PATH (reference, PROVISIONAL; stated in THIS chapter before Ch13): inscription architecture — the perception of how a MADE system is put together: which mark bears load and which is ornament; whether a sequence RECORDS (describes) or INSTRUCTS (commands); where a constructed pattern would fail. Civil face: authentication and restoration. Technique: contact or close attention to an inscribed surface — Cleon's 'seeing the bones of a thing'. LIMITS (charter §6.1, stated by Cleon on the page): reads STRUCTURE, not MEANING — it can say a passage is an instruction and cannot say what it instructs; works on MADE systems only (inscriptions, worked stone, constructed patterns), never on living architecture; costs attention and time, not reserve; useless in a fight. Cael WITNESSES the work at close range as labour (he holds sheets, moves the lamp) — Continuity Rule 6 for Ch13.

THE FINDING (before the reveal): the carvings on the three floors are NOT decorative and NOT commemorative — they are structured like instructions, the working notation of a made system; Karis has the strata and the stakes-and-alignment; Cleon has the scripts and thirty years; between them they establish the instruction-structure and NOT its content. Cleon's decade-old 'piece': a Deepstacks text fragment in an unconverted hand whose structure matches a carving's — matched now for the first time.

SEALED: no [UNBOUND] content; no 'Architect' beyond the citation's word (do not use it here); no 'built the system'; the reveal (the Fractured Path predates the system; the designer; 'four hundred years') is Ch15; 'built the same way twice' is the card's fixed line and refers to the SITES (the floors) — nothing about Paths or Arbiters; no still place; no six years.

BROM'S WANT: a Treswick merchant (unnamed; a broker's factor in the outer district) sees Iron Skin work — where? Brom does not declare inside walls by Oryn's order (the shoulder) — so the merchant sees the man's size and a load carried, or an old circuit reputation? Stage it as: the merchant sees Brom carry (a mule's load, a cart righted by hand, no Path) and knows a Copper's paper when he sees a man who has it, and offers a guard's post — a wage, a tier that matters here, a pass to the second tier — the life his family wanted, clean. He declines by going back down the hole with a box. One exchange with Cael later: 'You think Karis is right? That it's all built on something?' / 'I think we're about to find out.' / 'Good. I'd hate to have turned down a real job for a wrong hunch.' (fixed).

SELN'S SCENE (about him, nobody else; Cael's POV must witness it or its edges): the cache (B4–7: intelligence carried, unopened, targeted once at the Stair, kept); Treswick the first governed city since he defected; the registry up the hill would pay for its contents; he walks the tiers alone at night — HOW, with no pass? The unranked district's edges; the stairs at night unwatched; his tradecraft — and comes back down having decided nothing, seen by nobody, and lets Cael see that. No dialogue needed beyond a line.
Vastin down in the stacks as a hand, being nobody, badly; Lira a hand; the promise stands; nothing at the station.
Never 'Halcenvane', 'Velmere', 'Wray', 'Bracken'; no modern idiom; no meta-voice; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; 'upside down' 0; capped phrases 0; READER STANDARD (Gate 27).

purpose: The scholarship chapter — the carvings become instructions — with three wants served: Karis's (the work), Brom's (a clean ranked job offered and declined by going back down the hole), and Seln's OWN scene (Treswick is the first governed city he has stood in since he defected; the cache on his back; a registry up the hill that would pay for its contents in a currency he no longer takes; he walks the tiers alone at night, reads the station's light from the unranked district, comes back down having decided nothing and having been seen by nobody, and lets Cael see that he has decided nothing). Cleon's Rune Path shown in its civil face and its LIMIT stated by him plainly before Ch13's integration: 'I can tell you these are orders. I can't tell you what they order. For that you need the language, and the language is in the text, not the stone. That's her work, not mine.' Cael is IN the stacks as labour and witnesses the Rune work (Continuity Rule 6). Close on the fixed dialogue: 'This is the documentation of something. Somebody wrote these down so the thing could be built the same way twice … I don't think you're going to like what you've found, Karis.'

scene_shape.opening_state: The third and fourth days down: Cleon and Karis at the table with the three sets and the text he has kept for a decade, working a mark at a time; Cael holding sheets and moving the lamp; Brom and Lira with nothing to carry until the bell; Vastin on the knee, learning to be nobody.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Cael wants to watch the instrument that reads how things are built, at arm's length, on the carvings — not on himself — and to learn its limit before he wants it.
scene_shape.opposition: The carvings' language (unreadable); Rune's own limit (structure, not meaning); the bell; a merchant's clean offer to Brom; the cache on Seln's back in a city with a registry.
scene_shape.turn: Cleon's demonstration on a sheet, with the text beside it: the bones of a carving read aloud as structure — 'this mark bears the others; this one's ornament; this run commands, it doesn't describe' — and the limit said plainly: he can tell they are orders and cannot tell what they order. Then the match: his decade-old fragment's structure and the Hall's fourth sheet, the same bones.
scene_shape.choice: Cael does not ask Cleon to read him. He watches an instrument for made things and understands, against the rock, that a thing which reads only what was built cannot be turned on a man — and notes that he wanted it to be, and does not say so.
scene_shape.outcome: The carvings established as instructions; Brom's offer declined by a box; Seln's night walk decided nothing; Cleon's last words.
scene_shape.closing_state: DIALOGUE — the card's fixed close verbatim and contiguous: Cleon, late, over a carving-copy and a matched fragment: "You've been reading the strata. Old, older, oldest — I know, I read your face, you've dated these past anything the Compact admits." (he taps the text) "Here's what the strata can't tell you. These aren't the ruins of something. This is the documentation of something. Somebody wrote these down so the thing could be built the same way twice." (he sits back) "In thirty years I never had the stone to match the text. You walked in with three floors." A beat. "I don't think you're going to like what you've found, Karis. I've had a piece of it for a decade and I've never once slept well since." The file ends on that line.

must_include: Cleon's Rune work SHOWN in its civil face on a carving-copy with Cael present as labour (holding the sheet / the lamp) — the bones read aloud as structure; and the LIMIT stated by Cleon verbatim: "I can tell you these are orders. I can't tell you what they order. For that you need the language, and the language is in the text, not the stone. That's her work, not mine."

The finding established before the reveal: the carvings are not decorative and not commemorative; they are structured like instructions, the working notation of a made system; Cleon's decade-old text fragment matched to a carving for the first time.

BROM'S WANT-SCENE: a clean ranked offer (a guard's post, a wage, a tier) from a Treswick merchant who saw him carry, declined by going back down with a box — no speech; and the fixed exchange with Cael verbatim: "You think Karis is right? That it's all built on something?" / "I think we're about to find out." / "Good. I'd hate to have turned down a real job for a wrong hunch."

SELN'S SCENE, about him: the cache; the registry that would buy it; the tiers walked alone at night by his craft; the station's light read from below; back before dawn having decided nothing and seen by nobody; he lets Cael see he has decided nothing (a look, or one line).
Cael's understanding of Rune's limit as it bears on him (a thing that reads only what was built) — noted, not said; no request to be read.
Vastin as a hand, being nobody badly, one beat.
Close on the fixed dialogue VERBATIM and contiguous; the file ends on 'slept well since.'
READER STANDARD checked (banned words 0; conduct; no gore; no sexual content).

No Rune integration; no reading of Cael by Cleon; no still place.

allowed: Cleon's demonstration (which mark bears load; ornament vs command) in his own words; his decade-old fragment's physical form (a bound leaf? a board?) and its unconverted hand — described, not rendered.
The merchant/factor (unnamed) and the offer's terms (a guard's post at a broker's yard; a wage; a second-tier pass).
Seln's night route (the stairs unwatched at night; the walls' foot; a roof) — no gate passed by paper.
approval_required: Any new named person or place.
Any content of the carvings or the fragment beyond structure.
forbidden: Any meaning read from the carvings; any statement connecting the floors to Paths, Arbiters, or the Quieting's cause.

verified_findings.gate: Voice Charter §10; Craft Core 'Scene and summary'; packet obligations.must_include #3
verified_findings.evidence: He catalogued it afterward, from what Brom told him and what he saw, because it was Brom's and Brom told it in the fewest words a thing could be told in, and the fewest words were the whole of it. … A broker's cart had come into the ring road's yard at the inn's back, and had come through the yard's gate too fast … The broker's factor had watched him do it. … and had said so, and had made the offer at once, because a broker who sees a thing worth having does not wait.
verified_findings.consequence: The chapter's second designated want-scene never happens on the page. The card calls it 'a scene about him' and the packet calls it 'BROM'S WANT-SCENE'; the reader instead receives ~800 words of pluperfect report in which the cart is righted, the factor watches, prices, and makes the offer, all offstage, with a single line of direct speech ('I'll think on it'). The one moment the book exists to dramatize — a big, injured, decent man being handed the exact life his family wanted and choosing a box instead — is narrated rather than watched, and its charge is spent on Cael's summarizing rather th
verified_findings.repair_target: Stage the yard in real time from Cael's arrival: put Cael in the yard before the offer rather than 'at the end' (L65), and render the factor's offer as spoken dialogue with the terms named aloud, Brom's silence as the answer, and the box lifted while the factor is still talking. Keep L71's summarizing couplet ('Brom was offered the life. He picked up the box.') as the log line after the scene, not as its substitute. Retiring the pluperfect here recovers most of the words F-009 needs.

verified_findings.evidence: and that he had, for the length of a breath, been sorry, and that the sorriness was a thing he did not have a column for
verified_findings.consequence: A phrase the packet caps at zero appears once, and it appears in the chapter's most load-bearing interior paragraph — the one place a repeated series tic is most likely to be noticed and remembered. The cap exists because this construction reached watermark density in a sibling universe; the adjacent chapter already runs its cousin ('For the length of a man deciding whether…', ch10.md L39), so the family is accreting across consecutive chapters even though each individual chapter passes.
verified_findings.repair_target: Cut or replace the four words at L51. The sentence loses nothing: 'and that he had been sorry, and that the sorriness was a thing he did not have a column for' carries the same beat. Do not substitute a fresh repeated duration formula — §9 treats a replacement tic as the same defect.

verified_findings.evidence: He lay in the dark and had, from a man who said a thing once, the whole of the thing: that Seln had stood at night on the crown of a hill above the oldest registry on the Line, with the cache on his back and the station's pale light forty feet from him, and had looked at the door his old trade would have walked through, and had decided nothing, and had come back down, seen by nobody
verified_findings.consequence: Cael's only datum is four words spoken in a dark room; the sentence nonetheless hands him a measured distance ('forty feet'), a light's quality ('pale'), a specific vantage ('the crown of a hill'), a door, and the fact that nobody saw. Presented as 'the whole of the thing' rather than as inference, this is the narrator's knowledge wearing the viewpoint's clothes — and it is conspicuous precisely because L93, six lines earlier, models the disciplined handling of the same material. A reader who has been taught by this book that Cael writes down only what he can verify will feel the seam.
verified_findings.repair_target: Re-cast L99 as inference in Cael's own idiom: keep 'decided nothing', 'came back down' and 'seen by nobody' as what the one line proves, and demote the physical staging ('forty feet', 'the crown', 'the station's pale light') to what Cael supposes — the same move L93 already makes. Alternatively give Cael a witnessed anchor (grit on a boot, the cold on Seln's coat) so the supposition has a foot on the ground.

verified_findings.evidence: that Seln had stood at night on the crown of a hill above the oldest registry on the Line, with the cache on his back and the station's pale light forty feet from him
verified_findings.consequence: The packet's image is a man beneath the thing, reading its light from the unranked district — the geometry that carries the chapter's argument about who stands where in a tiered city, and that keeps an Arbiter station at the safe distance the party's whole Treswick discipline depends on (Cael has not set foot on the square; the station is a thing to be walked wide of). Standing Seln on the crown at forty feet inverts it: it puts him level with the station, spends the walk's tension on proximity instead of on the reading, and quietly makes his night riskier than the packet designed it to be.
verified_findings.repair_target: Move the reading of the station's light to below the walls — the unranked district, the stairs' foot, a roof — so that Seln reads the light up rather than standing beside it. The registry's door he 'would have walked through' can stay as the thing he has located from underneath. Reworking this alongside F-003 lets one revision serve both.

verified_findings.gate: Charter §2.8 (Injury Persists); progression module editor gate 2
verified_findings.evidence: had set the box down, and put his shoulder to the cart's bed, and put it back on its wheels. Alone. Without a Path, because a healer had said not a door, not a box, not a man, and Brom kept a price; with the good shoulder and his back and his legs, which was enough, because Brom had been big before he was anything else.
verified_findings.consequence: A man with a bound shoulder under a healer's standing order and a punctured foot rights a loaded cart by hand, alone, and pays nothing — no shake, no stagger, no favouring, and he is carrying a box up the yard inside the same beat. The book's own economy is exact about this cost everywhere else (Ch09 makes a point of what he does not say about three tiers on that foot; Ch12's state has the good shoulder used wrong and ledgered). Leaving the feat free undercuts the very discipline the scene is meant to honour — that Brom keeps the healer's price — and hands the reader a strongman moment in a se
verified_findings.repair_target: Ledger the cost in one or two clauses at L59 or in Cael's observation at L65: the good shoulder paid for it, the foot took the brace, and Brom sets the box on the other side afterward. Ch12 opens with 'the good shoulder used wrong', so a debt entered here is paid there rather than invented there.

verified_findings.evidence: He had wanted, against a post two days from here, an instrument for what did not move.
verified_findings.consequence: The post is neither two days' walk nor two days back. Ch07 dates it the 281st ('Two hundred and eighty-first day. The last post short of the river.') and Ch08 has the party crossing the bridge into Treswick at first light on the 282nd — one day's travel — while the chamber scene is the 286th, five days later. Whichever way a reader takes 'two days from here', the arithmetic of a book that dates every leg in its logs fails, and it fails on the sentence that carries Ch7's payoff.
verified_findings.repair_target: Replace 'two days from here' with a formulation that survives both readings — 'against a post across the river', 'against a post on the road in', or a corrected count ('five days back'). The payoff needs the post identified, not measured.

verified_findings.evidence: and it had walked, three days ago, into the first governed city Seln had stood in since he had walked out of one with it
verified_findings.consequence: Treswick was entered on the 282nd; the night walk follows the third day down (L7, the 286th) and precedes the fourth (L111), so four to five days have passed, not three. Small, but the series stakes its credibility on counted days and this narrator is the one who counts them.
verified_findings.repair_target: Correct to 'four days ago' (or drop the count and write 'this week') at L89, reconciled against whatever day the night walk is fixed to when F-011 is resolved.

verified_findings.evidence: "Good." Brom shifted the box. "I'd hate to have turned down a real job for a wrong hunch."
verified_findings.consequence: Exact-string comparison of the four fixed lines returns FOUND for three and MISSING for this one: the words are all present and in order, but an action beat is inserted mid-line, so the fixed unit is not reproduced. The reader consequence is small — the beat is well judged — but the packet's fixed lines are the one thing the seat is not licensed to reshape, and letting a split pass here weakens the rule for the fixed close.
verified_findings.repair_target: Either restore the line unbroken at L79 and move 'Brom shifted the box.' before or after it, or record the split as an approved variance in the run's exception log so the next exact-string check does not re-open it.

verified_findings.gate: Voice Charter §10 density check; packet output.target_words 4600 ±15%
verified_findings.evidence: By the third day down he had learned the lamp. … I've had a piece of it for a decade and I've never once slept well since.
verified_findings.consequence: 3,907 prose words counted by the method used on Ch09 and Ch10 (title line and the six rule separators excluded) — three words under the 3,910 floor, 15.1% under target; whole-file wc -w is 3,918, eight words over. The shortfall is trivial in itself and would not be worth a finding alone, but it sits on top of F-001: the chapter is at the floor precisely because the beat that should have been staged was reported instead, so the count is the symptom and the summary is the cause. The author report concedes the position ('Word count ~3,9xx — at the floor').
verified_findings.repair_target: Do not pad. Recover the words by staging the yard (F-001) and, if more is wanted, by spending the invention budget's licensed material on Seln's route (the stairs unwatched at night; the walls' foot; a roof) while repairing F-003/F-004. Either route lands the chapter comfortably inside the band.

verified_findings.evidence: and on the face, cut in with something finer than a chisel, lines. Not letters. He knew the Compact's letters and had seen four scripts that were not the Compact's on the shelves in three days, and these were none of the five
verified_findings.consequence: The board is flatly declared 'Not letters' in Cael's catalogue and is then, thirty lines later, a text 'in a hand I can half read' whose words are Karis's work — and the fixed close names it 'the text' Cleon never had the stone to match. The intended reading (Cael does not recognize a script that Cleon partly does) is available but is not signalled, so a careful reader is left holding two incompatible descriptions of the one object the chapter's finding rests on.
verified_findings.repair_target: Soften L9 to Cael's fallibility rather than a verdict — 'Not letters he knew' / 'Not letters, so far as he could tell' — or have Cleon at L39 name the gap explicitly ('It's a hand. You wouldn't know it; I half do'). One clause anywhere in the chapter closes it.

verified_findings.evidence: Late on the fourth day, with the bell an hour off and the lamp low, Cleon put the Hall's fourth sheet beside the board for the last time that day
verified_findings.consequence: The chapter's clock runs the third day down (L7, the 286th) and the fourth (L111, L123) — two days where the packet declares three, and where the STATE_RUNNING row written for this chapter claims the 286th–289th. Cleon's 'Give me a week' from Ch10 therefore advances by two days in the chapter that exists to spend that week, and the running state and the prose will disagree on the date Ch12 opens from (the 290th).
verified_findings.repair_target: Either carry the chapter to the fifth day down (the 288th) — the Seln night and the Vastin beat are both undated and could sit there — or reconcile the packet's span and the STATE_RUNNING row down to the 286th–287th before Ch12 is packeted, so the 290th still lands where Ch12's log says it does.
